column2: Melanin Is Not Required for Turgor Generation but Enhances Cell-Wall Rigidity in Appressoria of the Corn Pathogen Colletotrichum graminicola
column9: IDENTIFIED VIA WEB SEARCH ON THE ACCESSED DATE; ABSTRACT AND SEARCH-SUMMARY LEVEL ONLY, FULL TEXT NOT RETRIEVED. Registered so the claim it supports can be marked needs_verification rather than asserted. Reading it is the work that closes that. Supports: melanin is NOT required for turgor generation in C. graminicola; albino mutants failed to penetrate intact leaves and ruptured, but DID penetrate ultrathin PTFE membranes. Does NOT support the general 'melanin builds turgor to punch through' account, which it contradicts for this species.

column2: Comparative Transcriptome Analysis Reveals the Effect of the DHN Melanin Biosynthesis Pathway on the Appressorium Turgor Pressure of Colletotrichum gloeosporioides
column9: IDENTIFIED VIA WEB SEARCH ON THE ACCESSED DATE; ABSTRACT AND SEARCH-SUMMARY LEVEL ONLY, FULL TEXT NOT RETRIEVED. Registered so the claim it supports can be marked needs_verification rather than asserted. Reading it is the work that closes that. Supports: DHN-melanin knockouts reduced appressorial expansion pressure from 13.02 +/- 1.54 MPa to 7.34 +/- 1.23 and 9.34 +/- 2.22 MPa, with 1,8-DHN melanin described as a permeability barrier raising solute concentration. NOTE THIS DISAGREES WITH LUDWIG_2014 on whether melanin bears on turgor; different species, and the disagreement is the finding, not a detail to average away.
